clue.text: Dance exercise starting on time …

parts.note: a prom is a formal school dance, especially in America
PT is physical training, school exercise

explanation.surface: A dance class whose exercise routine opens the session, continued into the next clue by the dots.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this clue to the next: 'starting' here pairs with 'ending' there, and is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone punctual arrives exactly when expected, so being on time is a synonym.

clue.text: Place teacher, not the head, as cover for break

indicators.note: not the head means the teacher word drops its first letter

parts.note: a master is a schoolteacher

explanation.surface: A deputy teacher, not the head, covering during a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' is a broken bone, not a school break.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaster cast covers and protects a broken limb while the fracture heals.

clue.text: Two forwards crush one that may be in the soup

definitions.text: that may be in the soup

indicators.note: crush means the pair squeeze the numeral between them
Two asks for the forwards word written out twice

parts.note: on means forwards, as in moving on
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A rugby scene: two forwards flattening a player who is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' also means in trouble, so the surface sounds like a rugby tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent bulb is a common ingredient chopped into soups and stews.

clue.text: Cat finally loth to stop longer

indicators.note: to stop means the last letter plugs a gap in the longer word

parts.note: a panter is one who pants or longs for something

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of loth is taken

explanation.surface: A cat who is finally reluctant to hang around any longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'longer' is not 'for more time' but one who longs; H goes inside PANTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A leopard or puma, especially a black one, is a big cat of this name.

clue.text: … ending in breaking plate

indicators.note: the word in breaks into the plate, splitting it apart

parts.note: a fish (as in fishplate) is a metal plate bolted across a joint between rails

explanation.surface: Continuing the dots, a dance session closes with someone smashing a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: A fish, or fishplate, is the steel plate joining two railway rails; 'breaking' puts IN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The close or conclusion of anything is its end, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Come in to join her: I take part

indicators.note: part means only a portion of the run join her I take is used

explanation.surface: An invitation to come in and join someone, with the speaker taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'joIN HER I Take'.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into money or property is to receive it as a legacy after someone's death.

clue.text: I serve in US army: never would I work for Walt?

parts.note: I'm a GI, an American private soldier
ne'er is a poetic contraction of never

explanation.surface: A US soldier swearing he would never work for Walt.
explanation.walkthrough: The Disney company calls the designers of its theme-park attractions by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney's creative engineers who design park rides carry this coined title, so such a person works for Walt.

clue.text: Here one may learn from a bible in stiff cover

indicators.note: in places the bible letters inside the hard binding

parts.note: a hard cover is the stiff binding of a book
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Learning from a hardback Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League university in Cambridge, Massachusetts is a place of learning.

clue.text: Magazine's good year overcoming financial problems

indicators.note: overcoming means the good-and-year letters sit over and around the financial setback

parts.note: a loss is a financial setback

explanation.surface: A magazine having a good year despite its money troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiny-papered periodical is called by this name, from its coated paper.

clue.text: Citizen poking about there at show house

parts.note: a national is a citizen of a country

indicators.note: poking about suggests rummaging the letters of there at into a new order

explanation.surface: A citizen nosing around a venue where a show is on.
explanation.definitionFit: London's state-funded playhouse on the South Bank is a house for staging shows.

clue.text: A number in school in bad odour …

indicators.note: in places the number within the school letters

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: Someone in a school is in disgrace, with the dots leading on to an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' is a link; 'in bad odour' also reads as being in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong unpleasant smell or reek is exactly what this word names.

clue.text: … getting through exam, almost grumpy about it

indicators.note: about means the shortened grumpy word goes around the exam
almost means the word for grumpy loses its final letter

parts.note: surly means grumpy, bad-tempered
a viva is an oral examination

explanation.surface: A student scraping through an exam while grumbling about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry on from the previous clue; 'it' points back to the exam and is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming through a danger alive is to survive it, so the noun means pulling through.

clue.text: House an actor may have in his pocket

definitions.meaning: a house is a piece of real estate, a building owned

definitions.text: an actor may have in his pocket
definitions.meaning: a prop, the full word for which is a stage item an actor handles, small enough to pocket

explanation.surface: A house that an actor could carry in his pocket, which is plainly impossible.
explanation.walkthrough: Stage props are short for theatrical property; the second reading is the stage sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Real estate is owned land and buildings; on stage, a prop is any object used by actors.

clue.text: As capital, bad smell about yen, a principle for the Chinese

indicators.note: about means the smell surrounds the currency letter

parts.note: pong is British slang for a bad smell
Y is the symbol for the yen
yang is the active male principle in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: A capital city described by its smell, its currency and Chinese philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: North Korea's seat of government is this city, its capital.

clue.text: Country-style nickname Alice could give either twin?

definitions.meaning: dressed in rough woollen cloth like a country squire

definitions.text: nickname Alice could give either twin?
definitions.meaning: the Looking-Glass twins are Tweedledum and Tweedledee, so a pet name for either would shorten their shared first part

explanation.surface: Alice inventing a rustic nickname for one of two identical twins.
explanation.walkthrough: Alice meets Tweedledum and Tweedledee in Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty rural types wear woollen cloth from the Scottish Borders, so the adjective means rustic in manner.

clue.text: Snooty chap astride flanks of horse, lining up for this?

indicators.note: astride means the snooty chap straddles the horse's outer letters, as a rider does

parts.note: a toff is an upper-class, snooty man

indicators.note: flanks are the sides, so the outer letters of horse are taken

explanation.surface: A posh rider sitting on a horse, ready in line for the race.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the start of a horse race, when runners line up.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing the start is called by this phrase, and horses line up awaiting it.

clue.text: What a reverse — a big defeat — don't interrupt!

indicators.note: reverse means the word for what? is turned round

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what?
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: Someone shocked by a crushing defeat, insisting on finishing their account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What a reverse' looks like an exclamation over a setback; 'reverse' turns EH round.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen to someone until they finish speaking is the opposite of cutting them off.

clue.text: Being nauseating fouls me up

indicators.note: up as in messed up signals the letters of fouls me are disturbed

explanation.surface: Something sickening that leaves the speaker in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise that is excessive and cloying is sickening, so the word means nauseating.

clue.text: Why film star may get fat?

definitions.text: Why film star may get fat?

parts.words: Why film star may get fat?
parts.note: split the name into two words: someone whose food regime is lavish will put on weight

explanation.surface: Wondering why a film star might gain weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Marlene Dietrich was a German-American screen star; her surname splits as DIET RICH.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene of The Blue Angel was a Hollywood screen legend, and a lavish eating plan explains weight gain.

clue.text: Animal in River by Turner

parts.note: the Don is a river in Russia and in Yorkshire
a key is something turned in a lock

explanation.surface: An animal in a river scene painted by J M W Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like the painter, but it is something that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: The ass or burro is a domesticated beast of burden, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Play and blow for time

definitions.meaning: a drama by Samuel Beckett of this title
blowing the whistle for time finishes the match

explanation.surface: A referee blowing the whistle for time in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Beckett wrote this one-act drama; the final whistle closes a match.

clue.text: How one might briefly describe the Princess Royal's body?

parts.words: How one might briefly describe the Princess Royal's
parts.note: Princess Anne is King Charles's sister; shortened, that is Chas's sis

explanation.surface: A question about how to describe Princess Anne's figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Princess Royal is Anne, sister of Charles; 'briefly' shortens both names to CHAS'S SIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The frame or bodywork of a vehicle, and slangily a person's physique, is called this.

clue.text: Mammal long suffering in agony

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters within the agony word

parts.note: pain is agony

indicators.note: suffering suggests the word long being damaged into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An animal that has suffered for a long time in great agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long suffering' reads as one phrase, but 'suffering' is the anagram signal on LONG.
explanation.definitionFit: This scaly anteater of Africa and Asia is a mammal, an example of the class.

clue.text: If B was Brown and C was Cameron … oh dear!

parts.words: If B was Brown and C was Cameron
parts.note: listing prime ministers alphabetically, Brown then Cameron, the next letter is the next leader

explanation.surface: Musing on a list of British prime ministers, ending in a groan.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown, David Cameron and Theresa May were successive UK prime ministers, so D IS MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of consternation like this expresses alarm and distress at bad news.

clue.text: Thoroughly search small playing area? Not quite

indicators.note: Not quite means the playing area word loses its last letter

parts.note: a court is a playing area for tennis or squash

explanation.surface: Searching for a small playing area that isn't quite big enough.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area thoroughly in a hunt for something is a synonym.

clue.text: Venue that may offer pleasure? O, hooray!

indicators.note: may offer hints that these letters can be offered up in another form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A venue giving pleasure, greeted with a joyful cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is a link; PLEASURE, O and HOORAY are shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: Covent Garden's opera and ballet theatre in London is a famous performance venue.

clue.text: Bouncer's horse in dead heat, right?

indicators.note: in puts the horse inside the dead heat

parts.note: a tie is a dead heat, a race with no winner
gee-gee, GG, is a child's word for a horse

explanation.surface: Someone checking whether their horse finished in a dead heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' is not a doorman but the bouncy tiger in Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne's tiger from the Hundred Acre Wood is forever bouncing about.

clue.text: Teacher with degree pulled back out of the rubble

indicators.note: pulled back means the teacher-and-degree letters are read from the end

parts.note: sir is how pupils address a male teacher
BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree

explanation.surface: A qualified teacher being dragged out from under fallen rubble.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken fragments and remains left after destruction are a synonym for rubble.
